Aecora Silverfire.name: Aecora Silverfire
Aecora Silverfire.publicNotes: Los centauros son cazadores y rastreadores legendarios, semejantes a humanos muy musculosos unidos desde la cintura al cuerpo de poderosos caballos. Suelen ser reservados pero altivos, y asumen con rapidez que su fisico imponente y su larga historia de tradiciones culturales los hacen superiores a cualquier pueblo de dos piernas que encuentren. Aunque son bien conocidas las historias de choques sangrientos entre centauros y colonos humanoides, los centauros no son intrinsecamente sanguinarios ni temerariamente agresivos. Son orgullosos y obstinados, y no toleran bien a los forasteros que invaden sus tierras ancestrales.

Agai.name: Agai
Agai.publicNotes: Aunque los lideres de enclaves spriggan mayores suelen ser guerreros especialmente entrenados con habilidades muy especializadas, los senores de la guerra spriggan aprecian el armamento tradicional de estrella del alba y ballesta, valorando ese estilo de combate por su sencillez y porque aprovecha ambas armas al maximo. A menudo sirven como subcomandantes en grupos grandes, cumpliendo funciones similares a capitanes de la guardia o guardaespaldas de la realeza spriggan. En grupos pequenos o puestos remotos, un solo senor de la guerra spriggan suele dirigir una banda de matones spriggan.

Cuando Mantienes el conjuro, puedes mover cualquier numero de luces hasta 60 pies. Cada luz debe permanecer a 120 pies o menos de ti y a 10 pies o menos de todas las demas, o se apaga.

backpack->Bag of Holding (Type II).description:
la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.JBMBaN9dZLytfFLQ]

Aunque parece un saco de tela decorado con paneles de seda de colores vivos o bordados elegantes, una bolsa de contencion se abre a un espacio extradimensional mayor que sus dimensiones exteriores. El Volumen guardado dentro de la bolsa no cambia el Volumen de la propia bolsa de contencion. La cantidad de Volumen que puede contener el espacio extradimensional de la bolsa depende de su tipo.

Puedes Interactuar con la bolsa de contencion para meter o sacar objetos igual que con un saco corriente. Aunque la bolsa puede contener una gran cantidad de material, un objeto aun debe caber por la abertura del saco para poder guardarse en su interior.

Si la bolsa se sobrecarga o se rompe, se rasga y queda arruinada, haciendo que los objetos de su interior se pierdan para siempre. Si se le da la vuelta, los objetos de su interior se derraman sin sufrir danos, pero la bolsa debe volver a ponerse correctamente antes de poder usarse de nuevo. Una criatura viva colocada dentro de la bolsa tiene aire suficiente para 10 minutos antes de empezar a asfixiarse, y puede intentar Escapar contra una CD 13. Un objeto dentro de la bolsa no proporciona beneficios salvo que se recupere primero. Un objeto en la bolsa no puede ser detectado por magia que solo detecte cosas en el mismo plano.

Capacidad 50 Volumen

action->Enraged Growth.name: Crecimiento enfurecido
action->Enraged Growth.description:
Desencadenante El caudillo spriggan sufre dano.

Efecto El caudillo spriggan crece hasta tamano Grande, junto con su equipo, que vuelve a su tamano natural si se retira. Su alcance aumenta en 5 pies. Recupera [[/r 15[healing]]]{15 Puntos de Golpe} y obtiene un bonificador de estado +2 a los ataques cuerpo a cuerpo y a las tiradas de dano.

Este efecto continua hasta el final del siguiente turno del caudillo spriggan, pero en cualquier turno en el que inflija dano a otra criatura y no este @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigado}, el efecto se prolonga hasta el final del turno siguiente.

Cuando Crecimiento enfurecido termina, el caudillo spriggan queda fatigado durante 1 hora.

action->Shameful Memories.name: Recuerdos vergonzosos
action->Shameful Memories.description:
Si Akiros ve a otra criatura portar abiertamente el simbolo sagrado de Erastil, debe intentar una salvacion de @Check[will|dc:15]. A menos que falle criticamente la tirada de salvacion, queda temporalmente inmune a Recuerdos vergonzosos durante 24 horas.

Éxito crítico Akiros no se ve afectado.

Éxito Akiros se distrae por la verguenza y queda @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Indispuesto 1} durante 1 asalto.

Fallo Akiros queda @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Indispuesto 2} por su verguenza.

Fallo crítico Como un fallo, pero Akiros tambien queda @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Aturdido 1}. No queda temporalmente inmune a Recuerdos vergonzosos y puede volver a verse afectado por esta debilidad; esto probablemente significa que tendra que intentar de inmediato la salvacion de nuevo cuando se recupere del aturdimiento.

action->No Escape.name: Sin Huida Posible
action->No Escape.description:
Desencadenante Un adjacent enemigo se aleja.

Efecto Akiros puede Zancadear up to his speed, siguiendo a la criatura desencadenante and manteniendola a su alcance durante todo su movimiento hasta que deje de moverse or Akiros has movido toda su Velocidad.

action->Rage.name: Furia
action->Rage.description:
la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.Ah5g9pDwWF9b9VW9]

Requisitos No estas @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigado} ni en furia.

Recurres a tu furia interior y entras en furia. Obtienes una cantidad de Puntos de Golpe temporales igual a tu nivel mas tu modificador de Constitucion. Este frenesi dura 1 minuto, hasta que no haya enemigos que puedas percibir o hasta que caigas @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Inconsciente}, lo que ocurra primero. No puedes dejar de estar en furia voluntariamente. Mientras estas en furia:

  • Infliges 2 de dano adicional con armas cuerpo a cuerpo y ataques sin armas. Este dano adicional se reduce a la mitad si tu arma o ataque sin armas es agil.
  • Sufres un penalizador -1 a la CA.
  • No puedes usar acciones con el rasgo concentracion salvo que tambien tengan el rasgo furia. Puedes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Buscar} mientras estas en furia.

Cuando dejas de estar en furia, pierdes cualquier Punto de Golpe temporal restante de Furia y no puedes volver a usar Furia durante 1 minuto.

action->Life Bloom.name: Floracion vital
action->Life Bloom.description: Cuando Akuzhail muere, su cuerpo estalla en un tumulto de vegetacion palpitante y energia vital en bruto. Todas las criaturas vivas en una @Template[emanation|distance:60]{emanacion de 60 pies} recuperan [[/r 12d6[healing]]] Puntos de Golpe gracias a esta energia. Una floracion de Lamashtu plenamente desarrollada surge del cadaver, pero no puede realizar acciones en este asalto. En el siguiente asalto, la floracion de Lamashtu entra en combate en el mismo punto del turno en el que Akuzhail perecio en el asalto anterior, pero queda @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Lentificado 1}. Al final del turno de la floracion, intenta una @Check[flat|dc:11]; con un exito pierde la condicion ralentizado 1 al comienzo de su siguiente turno.

action->Of Three Minds.name: De tres mentes
action->Of Three Minds.description:
Desencadenante Akuzhail falla o falla criticamente una salvacion de Voluntad.

Efecto Akuzhail repite la salvacion de Voluntad con un penalizador -4. Si falla esta segunda salvacion, puede hacer un tercer intento, pero con un penalizador -8. No puede hacer un tercer intento si el segundo fue un fallo critico.

action->Three Headed.name: Tres cabezas
action->Three Headed.description: Cualquier aptitud que amputaria una cabeza de quimera, como un impacto critico con un @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.6xaxxKfvXED6LfIY]{Arma vorpal}, amputa una cabeza al azar. Perder una cabeza no mata a una quimera mientras le quede al menos una, pero le impide realizar Golpes con la cabeza perdida o usar el Arma de aliento de esa cabeza.

action->Triple Opportunity.name: Triple Opportunity
action->Triple Opportunity.description: Una quimera obtiene 2 reacciones adicionales cada asalto que solo puede usar para realizar Ataques de oportunidad. Debe usar una cabeza distinta para cada reacción y no puede usar mas de una contra la misma acción desencadenante. Si pierde una de sus cabezas, tambien pierde una de estas reacciones adicionales.

action->Bloom Venom.name: Bloom Venom
action->Bloom Venom.description:
Tirada de salvacion @Check[fortitude|dc:29]

Duración máxima 6 asaltos

Etapa 1 @Damage[2d6[poison]] and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Debilitado 1}

Etapa 2 @Damage[2d6[poison]] and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Debilitado 2}

Etapa 3 @Damage[2d10[poison]], debilitado 2, and exposure to Lamashtu's bloom.

action->Breath Weapon.name: Arma de aliento
action->Breath Weapon.description: Akuzhail exhala una @Template[line|distance:60] de veneno desde su boca de serpiente que inflige @Damage[11d6[poison]|options:area-damage] de dano (@Check[fortitude|dc:29|basic|options:area-effect]). Akuzhail no puede volver a usar Arma de aliento durante [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Breath Weapon]]{1d4 asaltos}.

action->Frightening Rattle.name: Cascabel aterrador
action->Frightening Rattle.description: Akuzhail agita el cascabel del extremo de su cola para distraer y asustar a sus enemigos. Cualquier criatura a 30 pies o menos debe tener exito en una salvacion de @Check[will|dc:29] o quedar @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Asustado 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Asustado 2} con un fallo critico). Con un exito critico, la criatura queda temporalmente inmune al Cascabel aterrador de Akuzhail durante 24 horas.

action->Lamashtu's Bloom.name: Floracion de Lamashtu
action->Lamashtu's Bloom.description:
Aunque algunos PNJ quedan afectados por la maldicion de la floracion de Lamashtu durante las partes 1 y 2 de este capitulo, durante la parte 3 los PJ tambien pueden exponerse a ella. Aunque la floracion es en si misma una maldicion, mecanicamente funciona mas como una enfermedad y por ello posee ambos rasgos de afliccion. Mientras la maldicion persista, una criatura no puede recuperarse de la enfermedad, y eliminar la maldicion no elimina automaticamente el componente de enfermedad de la afliccion. Ambos elementos deben tratarse por separado antes de que una victima que sufra la Floracion de Lamashtu este a salvo. Como con todos los elementos de esta maldicion, matar a la floracion de Lamashtu en el area C10 elimina automaticamente esta afliccion.

Tirada de salvacion @Check[fortitude|dc:23]

Inicio 1 semana

Etapa 1 sin efectos negativos (1 dia)

Etapa 2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Debilitado 1} (1 dia)

Etapa 3 debilitado 1 y @Damage[2d6[poison]] de dano (8 horas)

Etapa 4 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Inconsciente} y @Damage[4d6[poison]] de dano (10 minutos)

Etapa 5 muerte; Especial: una criatura que muere por la floracion de Lamashtu explota en una rafaga de follaje del Primer Mundo y libera un monstruo. Esta criatura suele ser una bestia o dragon de baja Inteligencia entre nivel 7 y 9, segun el criterio del DJ.

action->Three-Headed Strike.name: Golpe de tres cabezas
action->Three-Headed Strike.description: Akuzhail realiza un Golpe con su pico de buitre, sus colmillos de serpiente y sus mandibulas de ciempies, cada uno con un penalizador -2 y contra una criatura distinta. Estos Golpes cuentan como un unico ataque para su penalizador por ataques multiples, y el penalizador no aumenta hasta que haya realizado los tres ataques.

la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-family-ability-glossary.Item.08egiRxOvMX97XTc]

Humana Mediana con puno +26 para 2d6+16 contundente, o tigre con Velocidad 30 pies y Luchar.

Luchar 1 El tigre realiza un Golpe de garra contra una criatura a la que esta agarrando. Si el ataque impacta, esa criatura queda @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Tumbado}.

La criatura licantropa cambia a su forma humanoide, hibrida o animal. Cada forma tiene un aspecto especifico y persistente. La forma natural de un licantropo autentico es su forma hibrida.

En forma humanoide, la criatura licantropa usa su tamano humanoide original, pierde sus Golpes de fauces y garras, y obtiene un Golpe cuerpo a cuerpo de puno que inflige dano contundente igual al dano cortante que inflige su garra.

En forma animal, su Velocidad y tamano cambian a los del animal, obtiene cualquier efecto especial de Golpe del animal que aun no tuviera, como Agarrar, y pierde sus Golpes con armas.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ChangeShape]

action->Critical Debilitating Strike.name: Golpe debilitante critico

Efecto El objetivo queda @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Debilitado 1} o sufre un penalizador de estado -10 pies a sus Velocidades, a eleccion de Alasen. Con un impacto critico, el objetivo tambien debe intentar una salvacion de @Check[fortitude|dc:34].

Éxito crítico El objetivo no se ve afectado.

Éxito El objetivo queda @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Lentificado 1} hasta el final del siguiente turno de Alasen.

Fallo El objetivo queda @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Lentificado 2} hasta el final del siguiente turno de Alasen.

Fallo crítico El objetivo queda @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralizado} hasta el final del siguiente turno de Alasen.

action->Mobility.name: Movilidad

El cazador obtiene un bonificador por circunstancia +2 a las pruebas de Percepcion para @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Buscar} a la presa y a las pruebas de Supervivencia para @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.EA5vuSgJfiHH7plD]{Rastrear} a la presa.

La primera vez que el cazador impacta a la presa designada en un asalto, inflige 1d8 de dano de precision adicional. El cazador tambien ignora el penalizador por realizar ataques a distancia dentro de su segundo incremento de alcance.

feat->Instinct.name: Instinto
feat->Instinct.description:
Tú channel tu rage through an instinct. Tú decide what tu instinct means to tu. It could be una criatura or symbol beloved by tu clan, or a purely internal source or filter of tu rage, such as a belief, curse, heritage, or state of mind. Each instinct grants an instinct ability, plus more abilities puedes gain via feats that list that instinct as a prerequisite. It also determines what dano tu resist with raging resistance and, at higher levels, increases the dano adicional tu deal when tu @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.classfeatures.Item.WZUCvxqbigXos1L9]{Rage}.

Each instinct lists acts that are anathema to it. Siempre que tu perform such acts, tu lose the instinct's abilities and any feats that list tu instinct as a prerequisite until tu spend 1 día of downtime re-centering yourself, though tu keep all of tu other barbarian abilities.

feat->Rage.name: Furia

feat->Giant Instinct.name: Instinto de gigante
feat->Giant Instinct.description:
Tu furia te concede la potencia bruta y el tamano de un gigante. Esto no significa necesariamente que veneres a los gigantes; podrias despreciarlos o incluso aspirar a abatirlos. Tambien podrias parecer un gigante a ojos de los demas por tu fuerza excepcional o por tus emociones y ego desmesurados.

Anatema

No afrontar un desafio personal de fuerza es anatema.

Aniquilador titanico (aptitud de instinto)

Puedes usar un arma construida para una criatura Grande si eres Pequeno o Mediano, tanto normalmente como mientras estas en furia. Si no eres Pequeno ni Mediano, puedes usar un arma construida para una criatura de un tamano mayor que el tuyo. Obtienes acceso a esta arma mas grande, de cualquier tipo de arma disponible normalmente durante la creacion del personaje. Tiene el Precio y Volumen normales para un arma de su tamano. Cuando blandes un arma asi en combate, aumenta tu dano adicional de Furia de 2 a 6, pero tienes la condicion @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Torpe 1} por el tamano poco manejable del arma. No puedes eliminar esta condicion torpe ni ignorar sus penalizadores por ningun medio mientras blandes el arma.

Aptitud de especializacionNivel 7

Aumenta el dano de Furia al usar un arma mas grande de 6 a 10; si tienes especializacion con armas mayor, aumentalo de 10 a 18.

Resistencia furiosaNivel 9

Resistes dano contundente y un tipo a tu eleccion entre frio, electricidad o fuego, elegido cuando obtienes resistencia furiosa.

Nota: debes aplicar manualmente Torpe 1 cuando entras en furia. Recuerda alterar el tamano de tu arma para asegurarte de que la aptitud de instinto funcione correctamente.

No puedes dejar de estar en furia voluntariamente. Mientras estas en furia:

  • Infliges 2 de dano adicional con armas cuerpo a cuerpo y ataques sin armas. Este dano adicional se reduce a la mitad si tu arma o ataque sin armas es agil.
  • Sufres un penalizador -1 a la CA.

alchemist Tu body has become accustomed to physical hazards and resistant to pathogens and ailments. Tu proficiency rank for salvacion de Fortalezas increases to maestro. When tu roll a success on a salvacion de Fortaleza, tu get a exito critico instead.

Magus Tu body is accustomed to physical hardship and resistant to a wide range of ailments. Tu proficiency rank for salvacion de Fortalezas increases to maestro. When tu roll a success on a salvacion de Fortaleza, tu get a exito critico instead.

Gunslinger Tu body has become accustomed to physical hazards and resistant to ailments. Tu proficiency rank for salvacion de Fortalezas increases to maestro. When tu roll a success on a salvacion de Fortaleza, tu get a exito critico instead.

champion, fighter, Gunslinger, Inventor, Investigator, Magus, monk, ranger, rogue, Swashbuckler: Has learned how to inflict greater injuries with the armas tu know best. Tú deal 2 dano adicional with armas and ataques sin armas in which estás an experto. Este dano increases to 3 if estás a maestro, and to 4 if estás legendario.

alchemist, bard, cleric, druid, Oracle, Psychic, sorcerer, Summoner, Witch, wizard Has learned how to inflict grave wounds with tu most practiced armas. Tú deal 2 dano adicional with armas and ataques sin armas in which estás an experto. Este dano increases to 3 if estás a maestro, and to 4 if estás legendario.

barbarian: Tu rage helps tu hit harder. Tú deal an additional 2 dano with armas and ataques sin armas in which tienes experto proficiency. Este dano increases to 3 if estás a maestro, and 4 if estás legendario.

Obtienes tu instinct's specialization ability. See specific instincts for more information.

Ancient Wisp.name: Fuego fatuo antiguo
Ancient Wisp.publicNotes: Bolas malevolas de luz coloreada, los fuegos fatuos rondan marismas y bosques solitarios donde atraen a viajeros desprevenidos hacia el peligro. Pueden variar el color y la iluminacion que emiten, y disfrutan imitando linternas oscilantes o fuegos lejanos para sacar de senderos seguros a quienes estan perdidos o desorientados. Tambien pueden extinguir por completo su luz para volverse invisibles, y les gusta hacerlo cuando sus victimas ya estan totalmente perdidas y han comprendido que la luz que se movia a lo lejos no las estaba guiando hacia la seguridad.

action->Glow.name: Glow
action->Glow.description: 20 pies. Un fuego fatuo es naturalmente invisible, pero brilla con una luz de color, proyecta luz brillante en el aura y se vuelve visible. Un fuego fatuo antiguo puede aparecer como un diminuto punto de luz.

action->Magic Immunity.name: Magic Immunity
action->Magic Immunity.description: A will-o'-wisp is immune to all conjuros except @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.HRb2doyaLtaoCfi3]{Faerie Fire}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.0qaqksrGGDj74HXE]{Revealing Light}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.gKKqvLohtrSJj3BM]{Force Barrage}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Oj1PJBMQD9vuwCv7]{Quandary}.

Requisito Un enemigo is under a fear effect or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yZRUzMqrMmfLu0V1]{Moribundo} within 15 pies of the will-o'-wisp.

Efecto will-o'wisp feeds on la criatura's terror. It regains [[/r 2d8[healing]]] Puntos de Golpe, and if it has Gone Dark, its glow reignites.

A will-o'-wisp can take esta accion only una vez por asalto.

action->Go Dark.name: Go Dark
action->Go Dark.description: The will-o'-wisp extinguishes its glow, becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible}. It can end este efecto with another use of esta accion. If it uses its shock attack while invisible, the arc of electricity lets any observer determine its location, making the will-o'-wisp only @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Escondido} to all observers until it moves.

Ankou Assassin.name: Asesino ankou
Ankou Assassin.languages: no puede hablar ningún idioma; telepathy 100 pies
Ankou Assassin.publicNotes: Los ankous son asesinos sombríos que sirven a poderosas criaturas feericas, o incluso a los Primigenios, semidioses del Primer Mundo. En las cortes de los Primigenios o de soberanos feericos poderosos, estos siniestros asesinos acechan en lo alto mientras esperan la llamada a la acción, amenazas implicitas semejantes a armas mortales colgadas como decoracion en un salon real. Los ankous nunca hablan en voz alta; cuando necesitan comunicarse, lo hacen con un susurro telepatico dirigido a la mente de la victima. Aunque su cuerpo esta hecho de una extrana materia carnosa, sus garras y los crueles garfios de sus alas son de hierro frio afilado como una navaja.

Barbtongued Wyvern.name: Barbtongued Wyvern
Barbtongued Wyvern.publicNotes:
A wyvern is a venomous drake with a well-earned reputation for impatience and aggression. As much as 15 pies long and weighing up to 1,000 pounds, a wyvern's resilient body allows it to crash talons-first into large prey without serious risk to itself. A wyvern uses its momentum to stun its target before injecting it with searing venom or carrying it over the side of a nearby cliff. Because a wyvern lacks the strength to haul its prey all the way to its nest intact, it is far more likely to lift and drop its victim over a gully or canyon and let gravity do its work before it descends to pick apart the carcass.

Conversation is of little interest to a wyvern, as la criatura normalmente speaks only to taunt its prey, issue territorial claims, or demand tribute. Even so, many wyverns enjoy grim humor and tales of violent acts, particularly if those acts were committed by the storyteller. A wyvern properly appeased with meat, entertainment, and treasure sometimes agrees to provide assistance ranging from giving directions to serving as a mount for a powerful humanoid. However, these arrangements rarely last more than a few weeks before the wyvern's pride, malice, or insolence inspires it to flee or even betray its aliados. Only the truly cruel can cow a wyvern into servitude for an extended period, as most wyverns are so self-interested that they go out of their way to avoid helping others.

Ravenous, bestial, and driven by instinct-drakes are primitive draconic monsters who bear a fraction of the terrifying might of their larger cousins but little (if any) of the cunning. While they're weaker, slower, and less inclined toward reason than dragons, drakes are nonetheless a menace to criaturas and settlements around them. Their propensity for forming raiding parties-small social groups fittingly called "rampages"-makes them all the more dangerous; a single rampage of river drakes can quickly lay waste to a waterside village, and roving rampages of desert drakes are a plague to caravan traders.

Drakes share a number of physical characteristics that unite them as one species despite their wide variety of habitats and abilities. For example, drakes lack forearms, leaving them only their formidable jaws and thick-scaled tails with which to attack if engaged at melee range. Most drakes would rather avoid close combat, however, preferring to use their breath armas to wreak havoc in wide swaths from comfortable distances while flying overhead. Finalmente, all drakes have small reservoirs of their ancestral draconic power that they can tap into to perform incredible feats of speed.

Bloom Wyvern.name: Bloom Wyvern
Bloom Wyvern.publicNotes:
A wyvern is a venomous drake with a well-earned reputation for impatience and aggression. As much as 15 pies long and weighing up to 1,000 pounds, a wyvern's resilient body allows it to crash talons-first into large prey without serious risk to itself. A wyvern uses its momentum to stun its target before injecting it with searing venom or carrying it over the side of a nearby cliff. Because a wyvern lacks the strength to haul its prey all the way to its nest intact, it is far more likely to lift and drop its victim over a gully or canyon and let gravity do its work before it descends to pick apart the carcass.

Conversation is of little interest to a wyvern, as la criatura normalmente speaks only to taunt its prey, issue territorial claims, or demand tribute. Even so, many wyverns enjoy grim humor and tales of violent acts, particularly if those acts were committed by the storyteller. A wyvern properly appeased with meat, entertainment, and treasure sometimes agrees to provide assistance ranging from giving directions to serving as a mount for a powerful humanoid. However, these arrangements rarely last more than a few weeks before the wyvern's pride, malice, or insolence inspires it to flee or even betray its aliados. Only the truly cruel can cow a wyvern into servitude for an extended period, as most wyverns are so self-interested that they go out of their way to avoid helping others.

Ravenous, bestial, and driven by instinct-drakes are primitive draconic monsters who bear a fraction of the terrifying might of their larger cousins but little (if any) of the cunning. While they're weaker, slower, and less inclined toward reason than dragons, drakes are nonetheless a menace to criaturas and settlements around them. Their propensity for forming raiding parties-small social groups fittingly called "rampages"-makes them all the more dangerous; a single rampage of river drakes can quickly lay waste to a waterside village, and roving rampages of desert drakes are a plague to caravan traders.

Drakes share a number of physical characteristics that unite them as one species despite their wide variety of habitats and abilities. For example, drakes lack forearms, leaving them only their formidable jaws and thick-scaled tails with which to attack if engaged at melee range. Most drakes would rather avoid close combat, however, preferring to use their breath armas to wreak havoc in wide swaths from comfortable distances while flying overhead. Finalmente, all drakes have small reservoirs of their ancestral draconic power that they can tap into to perform incredible feats of speed.

Bloom of Lamashtu.name: Bloom of Lamashtu
Bloom of Lamashtu.publicNotes:
A thick, green stalk with spiraling rows of thorns stands at the center of this enormous flowering plant. Each flower has a growing seed pod at its center, surrounded by vibrant petals in a wide variety of colors. Crafted after consecutive seasons of experimentation, prayer, and ritual, the bloom of Lamashtu is the triumph of the cultist Darivan and his Cult of the Bloom. The fiendish plant aids their effort to infect the humanoid population of the Stolen Lands and replace them with monstrous predators. While the Bloom of Lamashtu is intelligent and is capable of understanding Abyssal, it has very little interest in anything other than spreading its curse.

Cultivated to spread misery and violence, the bloom is quietly malevolent, growing its seeds as rapidly as it can. It is 12 pies tall and weighs 600 pounds.

Bloomborn Athach.name: Bloomborn Athach
Bloomborn Athach.publicNotes:
The towering and brutish giants known as athaches are reviled for both their monstrosity and their cruelty. Beyond an athach's filthy habits, this giant is made stranger by the gangly third arm that protrudes from their torso and ends in a twitching, long-fingered claw. Huge, tusk-like fangs descend from an athach's upper jaw and prop their mouth open, leaking long strands of viscous drool that is itself is a toxic venom and coats the athach's fangs.

Athachs despise civilization almost as much as they despise their own kind, and they delight in committing sadistic acts and terrorizing victims. An athach does not keep a traditional territory of their own, but rather wanders the hinterlands of settled territories until they find a suitably easy settlement of smaller humanoids to target. Once the athach has chosen their target, the giant establishes a hidden lair in a location like an abandoned farmhouse or cave, and from there they launch their reign of torment. After a few weeks of harassing, capturing, and torturing victims, the athach bores of their games. The giant then goes on a final rampage, destroying every dwelling and eating every criatura they can find. Sometimes, the giant allows a survivor or two to escape, forcing these terrified victims to spend the rest of their lives spreading word of the athach's fearsomeness.

Bog Mummy Cultist.name: Bog Mummy Cultist
Bog Mummy Cultist.publicNotes:
The cultural practice of mummifying the dead is not the only way a body can become preserved, nor is it the only route that gives rise to these disease-spreading undead monstrosities.

Bog mummies (also called peat mummies or mire mummies) rarely, if ever, leave their marshy realms. Less powerful than their more notorious artificialmente preserved kin, bog mummies are preserved not by agents introduced during rituals but by the natural elements present in the airless, acidic morass of a peat bog or muddy swamp. While corpses preserved in this manner can certainly rise from the mire as bog mummies as the result of a curse by fell powers or the directed influence of a necromancer, the vast majority of them animate from a seething need for vengeance or to pursue some dire agenda left unfinished at the time of death-often because la criatura was slain or otherwise betrayed. The NATURE of this emotional tie to life and the emotional power of the deceased compel unlife beyond death, while the preservative qualities of the bog within which the body was disposed of does the rest.

Although most bog mummies are motivated by vengeance, many fulfill their dark yearnings with general violence. Filled with wrath and hatred for the living, they mercilessly attack any criaturas vivas that dare to venture into their dismal domains. Their agonized moans echo over their putrid homes, driving away most natural life dwelling therein and often alerting travelers to the potential danger that lies beneath the surface.

Centaur Scout.name: Centaur Scout
Centaur Scout.publicNotes:
Centaurs are legendario hunters and trackers who resemble heavily muscled humans with the bodies of powerful horses from the waist down. They are normalmente reclusive but haughty, quick to assume that their handsome physiques and long history of cultural traditions make them superior to any two-legged folk they encounter. While stories of bloody clashes between centaurs and humanoid settlers are well known, centaurs are neither intrinsecamente bloodthirsty nor recklessly aggressive. Rather, they are proud and stubborn and do not take kindly to outsiders who encroach on their ancestral grounds, some of which have been ruled by centaurs for thousands of years. Against despoilers of NATURE who fail to heed their warnings, centaurs do not hesitate to use their finely honed hunting skills to inflict deadly wounds.

Centaurs train with armas as well as their heavy hooves, and the thunder of centaurs charging across the plains is often mistaken for a stampede or even an earthquake. Despite their insular NATURE, some centaurs form close alliances with elves, fey, gnomes, and isolated human communities. Such aliados are often surprised to learn the depths of centaurs' honor, pragmatism, and wilderness LORE. Rarely, a centaur leaves its tribe to travel the wider world. Such lone centaur wanderers more easily integrate into humanoid societies, but other centaurs are quick to assume that some dishonor led to their exile and thus give such vagabonds a wide berth.

Centaurs have incredible variation in their individual size and coloration. Their upper bodies are fairly similar within a tribe and even region, but their lower bodies-like those of horses-can vary widely from parent to child. Most centaurs are at least 7 pies tall and weigh more than 2,000 pounds.

Centaurs live in groups of dozens of members, normalmente led by an old, powerful seer or battle-hardened warrior who has carried out many noble deeds and earned a lifetime of respect from their comrades. The revered leader guides the habits of their entire group; a wise seer might encourage the tribe to roam far from civilization to preserve the ways of its ancestors, while an aggressive warrior might foster skirmishes with nearby humanoid settlements and even rival centaur groups.

Darivan.publicNotes: Darivan no encaja con la imagen clasica de un sectario de Lamashtu. Aunque es profundamente religioso, su poder magico no procede de su fe, sino de un vinculo con su pasado ancestral. El favor de una driada ayudo a su abuelo a escapar de una vida brutal y encontrar una nueva patria segura para su pueblo, pero Darivan nunca tuvo paciencia para esa historia. Para el, su legado de hechiceria y su fe siniestra son elementos separados; sin embargo, sus visiones recientes de la floracion de Lamashtu trayendo una nueva oleada de monstruos a las Tierras Robadas lo han impulsado con fuerza, mostrandole como su ascendencia feerica y su fe demoniaca pueden reforzarse mutuamente.

Defaced Naiad Queen.name: Defaced Naiad Queen
Defaced Naiad Queen.publicNotes:
Naiad queens rule over pristine wildernesses centered on untouched lakes or other bodies of fresh water. Bards' songs and artists' paintings of nymphs tend to depict naiad queens in their slightly more humanoid forms, which they don when they make the rare journey into civilized lands to garner aliados or gauge threats.

Most naiad queens treat those who respect their domains with kindness, but they are fierce and quick in eliminating enemigos. Their blinding beauty and breadth of offensive conjuros make naiad queens fierce opponents if forced into a fight.

Nymphs are a family of fey that take the form of beautiful humanoids with elven features and have a deep association with the natural world. The most common of their kind are the dryads, which are spirits that embody great trees, but many other kinds of nymphs exist, including naiads, who watch over bodies of water. All nymphs are guardians of some element of NATURE, normalmente a specific tree or pond, or even-in the case of nymph queens-whole forests or massive bodies of water

Though it appears to be a cloth sack decorated with panels of richly colored silk or stylish embroidery, a bag of holding opens into an extradimensional space larger than its outside dimensions. The Volumen held inside the bag no change the Volumen of the bag of holding itself. The amount of Volumen the bag's extradimensional space can hold depends on its type.

Puedes Interactuar with the bag of holding to put items in or remove them just like a mundane sack. Though the bag can hold a great amount of material, an object still needs to be able to fit through the opening of the sack to be stored inside.

If the bag is overloaded or broken, it ruptures and is ruined, causing the items inside to be lost forever. If it's turned inside out, the items inside spill out unharmed, but the bag must be put right before it can be used again. A criatura viva placed inside the bag has enough air durante 10 minutos before it begins to suffocate, and it can attempt to Escape against a DC of 13. An item inside the bag provides no benefits unless it's retrieved first. An item in the bag no puede be detected by magic that detects only things on the same plane.

Engelidis.name: Engelidis
Engelidis.publicNotes:
In naga culture, the foul-tempered, unkempt spirit naga holds a contemptible place similar to that of hags in humanoid cultures. Estos decrepit criaturas live out lives of solitude, sought out only by those who are foolish or brave enough to think they can benefit from the spirit naga's powers without paying a heavy price-for most who dare to show such hubris, the price is their own lives.

Spirit nagas seek out desolate ruins and places long associated with death and corruption. Estos sinister, serpentine beings can be found in abandoned graveyards, crumbled fortresses, rotting swamps, and blighted woodlands. Though they may know little of the actual history of such places, the nagas are nonetheless attracted to the psychic remnants of evil deeds and tormented spirits that remain within the earth and stones there.

Despite their hideous appearance and treatment as pariahs by other nagas, spirit nagas feel a profound pride in their abilities and even in their hermetic existences. They see themselves as connected to a greater force whose mysteries are revealed only to those who can cast off the trappings and morals of "civilized" SOCIETY. Even so, spirit nagas gleefully accept the worship of other criaturas willing to bow to their capricious whims. They often form cults around themselves, using their charm conjuros and rituals to ensnare the minds of a few key individuals who spread the nagas' foul influence throughout a community.

Nagas are identifiable by their serpentine bodies and strange, humanlike heads. All nagas have magical abilities and great INTELLIGENCE, which they combine to advance their own agendas.

Enormous Flame Drake.publicNotes:
Ravenous, bestial, and driven by instinct-drakes are primitive draconic monsters who bear a fraction of the terrifying might of their larger cousins but little (if any) of the cunning. While they're weaker, slower, and less inclined toward reason than dragons, drakes are nonetheless a menace to criaturas and settlements around them. Their propensity for forming raiding parties-small social groups fittingly called "rampages"-makes them all the more dangerous; a single rampage of river drakes can quickly lay waste to a waterside village, and roving rampages of desert drakes are a plague to caravan traders.

Drakes share a number of physical characteristics that unite them as one species despite their wide variety of habitats and abilities. For example, drakes lack forearms, leaving them only their formidable jaws and thick-scaled tails with which to attack if engaged at melee range. Most drakes would rather avoid close combat, however, preferring to use their breath armas to wreak havoc in wide swaths from comfortable distances while flying overhead. Finalmente, all drakes have small reservoirs of their ancestral draconic power that they can tap into to perform incredible feats of speed.

Evindra.name: Evindra
Evindra.publicNotes:
Nereids are aquatic fey with deep ties to water. They share some similarities with naiads, but they are not guardians and do not bind themselves to a specific body of water. Although they are primarily aquatic criaturas, their unique ability to imbue their vitality into a supernatural shawl allows them to travel on land as well. A nereid must be careful when manifesting a shawl, however, as their life essence is bound to it, so it can be stolen or destroyed to threaten the nereid.

Nereids prefer to exist in isolation. Left to their own devices, they avoid combat, but when forced to fight, their ability to transform the natural waters in their flesh into poison serves them as well as any arma.

Often, ignorant sailors lump all water-dwelling fey into a single category of "aquatic tempters", regardless of the fey's type or gender, using these criaturas' names interchangeably to represent the concept of a beautiful figure who exists to lure mortals to a drowning death. Whereas naiads have more patience and often seek to educate the ignorant regarding the harm that stereotypes can cause, nereids and rusalkas have little patience for such methods. Rusalkas are the primary source for the legends of fey preying upon sailors, and nereids loathe them for that, as they prefer to live apart from humanity and enjoy the beauty of the natural world in peace.

When a nereid learns of a rusalka's increased activity, it often seeks out the rusalka to route them-not so much out of an urge to protect humanoids (in whom nereids tradicionalmente have little interest), but to prevent the rusalka from inadvertently riling up violent responses from humanoids who no puede be bothered to note the difference between a murderous fey and one who just wants to be left alone.

Fetch Behemoth.name: Fetch Behemoth
Fetch Behemoth.publicNotes:
A fetch behemoth is much larger than a stalker, and forms from the soul of a Grande fey or humanoid.

A fetch is a twisted, deviant simulacrum of a humanoid criatura that exists or existed at one point on the Material Plane. Rumors of fetches that are reflections of entities from other planes persist, but none of these tales speak of fetches that duplicate anything other than a sapient source. A fetch can manifest spontaneously when a powerful criatura undergoes a significant emotional event or dies, either while on the First World or while in an area significantly influenced by the First World, but one can also be created by significant forces like the Eldest in order to torment and vex those who have annoyed them. While a fetch manifests from a soul's "reflection," and as such bears a striking resemblance to that criatura's appearance in life, a fetch has no true memories of its own. It keeps fragments of false remembrances from its source as if it experienced them in a half-remembered dream-which ensure the fetch is enraged by and jealous of its source.

A fetch is similar in appearance to la criatura whose soul spawned it, save that it often displays fey-like features such as pointed ears, plantlike elements, or supernatural grace. A fetch who seeks to impersonate a stillliving source must disguise these features, and takes care to manifest its fetch arma as one known to be wielded by its target.

When a fetch dies, it and its manifested items fades away into a bloom of plant life, its soul instantly recycled into the First World, leaving behind a patch of weeds and thorny flowers roughly in the shape they held in mockery while alive.
Fetch Behemoth.saveDetails: +1 de estado a todas las salvaciones contra magia

action->Bound to the Mortal Night.name: Bound to the Mortal Night
action->Bound to the Mortal Night.description: Unlike most ghosts, Fionn no esta bound to a specific site. Instead, his exile to the Material Plane has bound him to the night itself. He can travel anywhere he wishes, so long as it is night. During the day, he cannot travel further than thirty pies from the location he occupies as the sun rises. He cannot leave the Material Plane at all, and if he suffers an effect that would normalmente transport him to another plane, he remains on the Material Plane and instead queda @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Aturdido 3}.

la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-family-ability-glossary.Item.unR8VVR4yyRnsmnB]

In order to put Fionn permanently to rest, the PCs must release his brother Kean from Amiri's blade-doing so renders Fionn's plan to use Kean's soul to return to the First World impossible and causes the frustrated ghost to accept his fate and resign himself as well to the afterlife. Until this occurs, Fionn seeks out the blade each time he rejuvenates; now that he's seen the blade in person, he's capable of sensing its location at all times.

When a ghost is destroyed, it re-forms after [[/br 2d4 #days]]{2d4 days} within the location it's bound to, fully healed. A ghost can be permanently destroyed only if someone determines the reason for its existence and sets right whatever prevents the spirit from resting.

Una criatura that fails its save against the conjuro is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Anonadado 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Anonadado 2} con un fallo critico) by the overwhelming sensation and belief that they have been exiled from all they hold dear. Este stupefaction value cannot be reduced below 1 as long as la criatura continues to be affected by outcast's curse.

action->Fearsome Blizzard.description:

All criaturas vivas within @Template[emanation|distance:60]{60 pies} of Fionn debe intentar una @Check[fortitude|dc:33] salvacion. Fionn no puede use Fearsome Blizzard for [[/br 1d4 #Recharge Fearsome Blizzard]]{1d4 asaltos}.

Éxito crítico La criatura no se ve afectada.

Fallo crítico La criatura takes @Damage[20d8[cold]] dano, queda @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Asustado 2}, and queda @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Huyendo} as long as they remain asustado. The asustado and fleeing effects have the emotion, fear, and mental rasgos.

First World Army.name: Ejército del Primer Mundo
First World Army.description: Este army is composed of an eclectic mix of fey, beasts, and plants—a supernatural mob of monsters with a wide range of options in battle.

campaignFeature->Battlefield Adaptabilit.name: Battlefield Adaptability
campaignFeature->Battlefield Adaptabilit.description: The First World army has a wide range of criaturas in its ranks, and it can shift its tactics to support those with different mobilities. It can take esta accion to achieve one of the following benefits: Ignore ground-based difficult terrain, reduce @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.kingmaker-features.Item.oVhkdym3D6TiTbrN]{Mired} to 0, quedar @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.kingmaker-features.Item.tWS8aMCyeGKcnFh1]{Oculto}, or gain a +2 bonificador por circunstancia on Maneuver checks to Advance and to Disengage. The effect lasts until el comienzo de the First World Army's siguiente turno.

campaignFeature->Battlefield Adaptabilit.name: Battlefield Adaptability
campaignFeature->Battlefield Adaptabilit.description: El army obtiene el unique Battlefield Adaptability war action.

campaignFeature->Primal Magic.name: Primal Magic
campaignFeature->Primal Magic.description:
Requisito First World army is not @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.kingmaker-features.Item.2IqM1XHELKwARAx1]{Engaged};

Efecto First World army uses its primal magic against another army on the battlefield and debe intentar una Morale check against la mente del objetivo Morale DC. If they succeed, the First World army applies one of the following effects, determined randomly ([[/r 1d10]]), to el objetivo army.

1–2 Entangling Vines Coils of whipping vines grow out of the ground to entangle the army. The army increases its @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.kingmaker-features.Item.oVhkdym3D6TiTbrN]{Mired} condition by 1 (2 on a impacto critico).

3–4 Horrific Visions The soldiers' minds are assaulted with horrific illusions. The army increases its @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.kingmaker-features.Item.7LMDwpVijK7x5Jst]{Shaken} condition by 1 (2 on a impacto critico).

5–6 Primal Storm A churning storm cloud above the army strikes the soldiers dozens of times with bolts of lightning, inflicting 1 point of dano to the army (2 points of dano on a impacto critico). Until el final de the targeted army's siguiente turno, it functions as if in high wind and rain (see Battlefield Terrain Features on page 578).

7–8 Sensory Assault The soldiers become overwhelmed with strange lights or tricked by illusions. Until el final de su siguiente turno, the army takes a –2 penalizador por circunstancia on all attacks and Maneuver checks.

9–10 Overwhelming Magic Roll twice and apply both results, but the First World army suffers a –4 penalizador por circunstancia on its Morale check against el objetivo army's Morale DC.

campaignFeature->Supernatural Attacks.name: Supernatural Attacks
campaignFeature->Supernatural Attacks.description: Siempre que a First World army scores a impacto critico on another army, it increases that army's @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.kingmaker-features.Item.dmzpRlOrorEFUETl]{Weary} condition by 1 as their attacks cause some soldiers to become poisoned, fall asleep, shrink in size, or suffer other eerie side effects.

campaignFeature->Tactical Training.name: Tactical Training
campaignFeature->Tactical Training.description:
The First World Army can use the following tactical actions: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.kingmaker-features.Item.8wjiF3ctXUjP9oyX]{Counterattack}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.kingmaker-features.Item.G2eBcOnUHb3yT7JL]{Dirty Fighting}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.kingmaker-features.Item.Hi4LKGOKe6yMDOH5]{Feint}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.kingmaker-features.Item.ggVahjiAlVICpiPA]{Taunt}.

Note: Este tactic also grants the army a +1 bonus to attacks in order to keep its attack bonus in line with the statistics given in the Kingmaker adventure.

First World Army.publicNotes: Este ejército está compuesto por una mezcla ecléctica de hadas, bestias y plantas: una turba sobrenatural de monstruos con una amplia variedad de opciones en batalla.

Flooding Room.name: Flooding Room
Flooding Room.description: When the western secret door is opened or any of the trapdoors in the ceiling are forced open, the trap is triggered. As soon as this occurs, the portcullises to the east and west come crashing down, each consisting of solid iron sheets that form watertight seals. At the same time, the dozen 5-pies-wide trapdoors open in the ceiling. Estos holes are the mouths of winding tunnels that connect to a second pair of apertures on the submerged side of the island outside, allowing the waters of the Little Sellen River to plunge down into this room, possibly damaging or knocking @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Tumbado} those in the square portion of the room itself (but not in the adjoining hallway) and eventualiado flooding the entire chamber.
Flooding Room.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:26] (este increases a @Check[thievery|dc:30] once el trampa es activated) a disable one de el 12 trapdoors y seal ello shut; disabling todos 12 de el trapdoors completely deactivates el trampa, but un fallo critico en cualquier attempt causes el trampa a trigger; @Check[thievery|dc:24] a disable one de el watertight portcullises y prevent ello de falling; magia such as shape piedra o muro de piedra o even lock puede also be used a disable portions de este deadly trampa at el DJ's discretion
Flooding Room.reset: La trampa must be reset with a major engineering effort.
Flooding Room.routine:
(12 actions) La trampa loses 1 action for each of its 12 ceiling trapdoors that are disabled. On each of the trap's actions, it pours water into the room, filling it to a depth of one inch. If all 12 trapdoors are open, it thus fills the room at a rate of 1 pies per round. If one of the portcullises is breached, the trap fills the room at half the rate, and if both are breached, it fills at one quarter the rate. Once the cascade of water begins, it's easy enough for a PC to avoid the downpour, but any criatura that deliberately enters the cascade is subjected to the trap's Rushing Water reaction. If una criatura is struck by Rushing Water while already underwater, the result of its Reflex save is automaticamente improved one degree of success.

The flooding ends and the trap deactivates once the area is filled to the ceiling-at this point, the water's surface is at the level of the river, and at the top of the stairs leading down from areas D4 and D6. A Mediano or smaller criatura can try to Swim to freedom through one of the 5-pies-wide tunnels leading to the river from a trapdoor, but doing so requires navigating 200 pies of flooded tunnels.

action->Rushing Water.name: Rushing Water
action->Rushing Water.description:
Desencadenante secret door to the west or any trapdoor is opened.

Efecto 12 ceiling trapdoors open along with the two secret doors to the cyclops zombie alcoves, releasing river water and zombies into the room. Any criatura standing in the central 40-by-40 pies section of the main room debe intentar una @Check[reflex|dc:28] salvacion; the trap then rolls initiative.

Éxito crítico La criatura takes ningun dano.

Éxito La criatura takes @Damage[(1d10+6)[bludgeoning]] dano from the cascade of water.

Fallo La criatura takes @Damage[(2d10+13)[bludgeoning]] dano from the cascade of water.

Fallo crítico La criatura takes @Damage[(2d10+13)[bludgeoning]] dano from the cascade of falling water and is knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Tumbado}.

Foras.name: Foras
Foras.publicNotes:
El man who would reciben el name Foras grew up millennia ago among worshipers de Pharasma, yet el came a believe que el Outer Gods fueron el keys a claiming personal power. He tricked su people's priests into a imparting eldritch truths ellos would no normalmente share, then shared them con un few fellow secretive scholars de el oculto.

Gathering those whom Foras could manipulate, el retreated a un nuevo stronghold-un location now known as Candlemere. Here, Foras's cult gave up su sight y su souls, solo a quedan trapped con him dentro de su own compound cuando su leader's brother tracked them down y imprisoned them. Yet even este hasn't stymied Foras, y el continues a este dia a work toward su goal de drawing Yog-Sothoth into el world.

Freshly Bloomed Basilisk.name: Freshly Bloomed Basilisk
Freshly Bloomed Basilisk.publicNotes:
The basilisk is an eight-legged reptile with a nasty disposition and the ability to turn criaturas to stone with its gaze. Folklore holds that, much like for the cockatrice, the first basilisks hatched from leathery eggs laid by snakes and incubated by roosters, but little in the basilisk's physiology lends any credence to this claim.

A basilisk prefers to eat petrified flesh. Once a victim has been turned to stone, the basilisk crunches the fossilized corpse with its powerful jaws and lets its potent stomach acids do the rest. Este digestive process is extremely slow and inefficient, causing the basilisk to move so lethargicaliado that it appears as if in mid-petrification itself. Este has even led to the saying "as slow as a well-fed basilisk." Certainly basilisks are well-known for their slow gait and slothful NATURE, but a predator that can turn its prey to stone with a glance hardly has much need for speed.

An adult basilisk is 13 pies long from head to tail and weighs roughly 300 pounds. Estos reptiles make hissing sounds when moving about that turns to a guttural gurgle when they're agitated. Though they are normalmente solitary criaturas that come together only to mate and lay eggs, there are periodic reports of regions being infested with unusual numbers of basilisks. What causes these unusual congregations of basilisk activity is unknown.

For unknown reasons, weasels and ferrets are immune to the basilisk's stare, and they sometimes sneak into basilisk lairs while a parent is hunting in order to consume eggs or freshly hatched young. Some legends suggest that a basilisk's blood can transmute common stones into other material, but this is likely a case of witnesses misinterpreting the magical restoration of previously petrified criaturas or body parts.

If it fails and has not already been ralentizado by Petrifying Glance or esta aptitud, it queda @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Lentificado 1}. If la criatura was already ralentizado by esta aptitud or Petrifying Glance, a failed save causes la criatura to be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dTwPJuKgBQCMxixg]{Petrificado} permanently.

Una criatura petrified in this manner that is coated (not just splashed) with fresh basilisk blood (taken from a basilisk that has been dead no longer than 1 hora) is instantly restored to flesh.

A single basilisk contains enough blood to coat [[/br 1d3 #Mediano Las criaturas]]{1d3 Mediano criaturas} in this manner.

Gedovius.name: Gedovius
Gedovius.publicNotes:
Gargoyles are monstrous hunters made of elemental stone. They use their resemblance to decorative statues to hide in plain sight in cities during the day and descend upon unlucky pedestrians at night. Their most common form is that of a horned humanoid with bat-like wings, but individual gargoyles show a great deal of variation, with some appearing more or less humanoid and others resembling no known criatura. A gargoyle's features are not flxed; city-dwelling gargoyles who remain in the same locale long enough slowly morph, day by day, to match the style of the local architecture. Estos patient monsters can stay disguised for long stretches of time as they patiently await an opportunity to strike.

Gargoyles tend to be lone hunters, though sometimes they band into fearsome tribes called "wings" for protection or sport. On rare occasions, wings become relatively stable communities, and gargoyles in wings may even aliado with other criaturas such as demons and intelligent aberrations, though these alliances exist on a razor's edge. The majority of gargoyles are treacherous, vindictive, and petty-rasgos that preclude lasting partnerships. Many tend to be obsessive and compulsive. Some are collectors, focusing on anything from books to grim trophies, while others are ritualistic or overly passionate about niche intellectual subjects or certain artistic motifs. Estos tendencies often contribute to the dissolution of wings as individuals' obsessions and compulsions clash.

Grabbles.name: Grabbles
Grabbles.publicNotes:
Mitflits, also known as mites, are self-loathing and pitiful cowards, easily bullied into servitude by other criaturas or even slightly more powerful mitflit leaders. They tame insects, spiders, and other such criaturas to serve as faithful aliados. Mitflits have lost most of their ancestral gremlin magic, leaving these incomplete beings full of doubt and insecurity. Mitflits find companionship in the other base criaturas of the world, and forge bonds of friendship with vermin, the only other beings that seem willing to accept them. A social structure, even one in which they are bullied, partialiado fills the hole within mitflits' personalities, and they rarely rebel or rail out unless their rage hits a breaking point.

Gremlins are cruel fey tricksters and saboteurs who have fully acclimated to life on the Material Plane, finding distinct niches for their inventive destructiveness. All gremlins delight in ruining or breaking things, whether it's something physical like a device or vehicle or something intangible such as an alliance or relationship. A gremlin's greatest joy is watching the collapse of complex creations, preferably after the lightest and slightest, carefully targeted push from the gremlin. Gremlins tend to denigrate, bully, or even slaughter their lesser kin, particularly mitflits, whom gremlins (and many others) derisively call "mites."

Grigori.name: Grigori
Grigori.publicNotes:
El bard Grigori es un charismatic orator y un agent de Pitax who seeks a undermine el PJ' authority mientras spying en su kingdom. He shows up en el kingdom's capital city mientras el PJ son out adventuring y immediately begins giving speeches criticizing y denigrating su leadership y actions. More y more de el townsfolk gather a hear him talk y, as el dias wear en, el builds un wellspring de support among el disaffected settlers en el town. Every decision el PJ make tiene un winner y un loser, y Grigori es gifted at shifting focus a el losers en these decisions y riling them up. Whether ello es appealing a el citizens who didn't get what ellos wanted cuando el PJ built un nuevo city block, a spinning un narrative que paints un recent event en el most horrid light for those for whom el outcome fue un negative, un properly played Grigori should quedan un constant barb en el players' side y one de el most memorable villains ellos encounter. Grigori recibe great pains a avoid breaking cualquier de el PJ' laws so que ellos tienen no legal justification a arrest him otro than que ellos want a silence him.

Grigori es more than just un itinerant storyteller; el's un spy y agent provocateur sent by King Irovetti, el Lord de Pitax, a spread chaos y dissent en el town con el aim de overthrowing el PJ y possibly paving el way for Pitax a annex el settlement. In order a cobertura su rastros y retain plausible deniability, Irovetti used several layers de agents a hire Grigori; as far as el bard knows, el fue hired a cause trouble en este fledgling town by agents de Fort Drelev a el west.

Hannis Drelev.name: Hannis Drelev
Hannis Drelev.publicNotes:
Hannis Drelev spent his youth in Brevoy frustrated at the lack of opportunity for advancement. When he heard Lady Jamandi was looking for volunteers to aid her in exploring and taming the Stolen Lands, he saw an opportunity to bolster his fame. In the months since, Hannis has come to regret his decision, and now that he has been forced to surrender to Irovetti and Armag, his attitude has shifted from frustration to outright cruelty.

Drelev comes across as a sullen, greedy, conceited man, never satisfied with his lot in life, but always disdainful of anyone who has less than him. Though skilled at politics, the baron fancies himself a skilled swordsman as well. He loves dueling and often spars against his own guardsmen and senior officers. He likes to show off, taunting and belittling those he overpowers, but reacts angrily to situations where others get the best of him.

A patient opponent who prides himself on his ability to skillfully outmaneuver his enemigos, Baron Drelev begins nearly every turn with Defensive Slice. He favors disarming enemigos, and attempts to do so una vez por asalto when facing an armed enemigo, mocking them wickedly if he's successful and cursing them violently if not.

Hargulka.name: Hargulka
Hargulka.publicNotes:
Before his dreams were invaded and his ambitions enhanced by Nyrissa's eldritch manipulations, Hargulka had already established himself as a leader among trollkind, though his goals never reached beyond bullying his fellow trolls into rampaging the immediate environs for food and wealth to bring back to him as offerings. The notion of becoming a "king" never crossed his mind until he had a vivid, unforgettable dream of himself sitting atop a throne and basking in the fear and adoration of not only trolls, but hobgoblins, harpies, and all manner of slavering monsters-criaturas who might be viewed as dangerous enemigos but, to Hargulka, were now his loyal minions.

To Hargulka, the PCs' kingdom is rightfully his own. He intends to conquer them, claim their capital for himself, and dine on the flesh and bones of their citizens. Yet despite these violent goals, the troll knows better than to simply attack his enemigos mindlessly. Instead, he spends his time working with his loyal trolls to seek out like-minded monsters in the wilds to recruit them to his cause. As a result, the longer Hargulka remains in power, the more dangerous and aggressive the monsters of the Stolen Lands will become!

Quick-tempered and fond of violence, a hill giant gladly raids and pillages the defenseless but is quick to flee from those who are bigger, stronger, or better organized than they are. A hill giant is never above shoving or tricking one of their own kind to slow down their opponent or get the best loot.

Giants are massive humanoid criaturas who live in remote regions throughout the world. They are divided into a number of subtypes.

Con un exito, one uncauterized stump regrows two heads; con un exito critico, two uncauterized stumps regrow into two heads each. action->Head Regrowth.name: Head Regrowth

A hydra can regrow a severed head using Hydra Regeneración. Una criatura can prevent this regrowth by dealing acid or dano de fuego to the stump, cauterizing it. Single-target acid or fire effects need to be targeted at a specific stump, but effects that deal dano de salpicadura or affect areas covering the hydra's whole space cauterize all stumps if they deal acid or dano de fuego. If the attack that severs a head deals any acid or dano de fuego, the stump is cauterized instantly. If all five heads are cauterized, the hydra dies.

Ilthuliak.name: Ilthuliak
Ilthuliak.publicNotes:
Murderous tyrants of marshes, swamps, bogs, and fens, black dragons terrorize their domains with intense fervor. Gleefully sadistic, they rule their fetid principalities from a deep cave or otherwise isolated part of the swamp with a mix of lightning-quick raids and subterfuge. Their hatred for other criaturas is as acidic as their breath armas, and they rarely tolerate even other dragons of their kind-except perhaps to mate or temporarily collaborate to take down a mutual enemigo.

Black dragons are amphibious-although they breathe air, their gills also allow them to breathe water. Their frills and fins make them accomplished swimmers, well suited to their wetland environments and submerged lairs. They're immune to the fetid water that comes as a result of their magical ability to corrupt water.

Black dragon lairs are as foul as their souls. The floors are littered with rotting meat, and plundered treasures line the muck and slime of their dank caves amid twisted roots and creepers. Such places are often crawling with pests, snakes, and slimes. Though they claim natural caverns when they can, they make do with areas of dense, twisted vegetation within a swamp. Black dragon treasure hoards primarily consist of gems and expensive glass work, as valuables of softer substance no puede survive the dragon's acidic presence.

While there are many types of dragons, from the powerful planar dragons to the strange esoteric dragons, few dragon varieties are as well-known and as rightly feared as the chromatic dragons. Differentiated by the hue of their scales, each color of dragon unleashes its own flavor of murderous cruelty-be it by claw, tooth, or breath-and unlike most criaturas, dragons only become more powerful as they age. Their lust for treasure, food, bloodshed, and control are legendario. Physicaliado powerful with egos to match, these dragons are often moreunido depraved and act as criminal masterminds, vicious tyrants, or voracious raiders.

Immense Mandragora.name: Immense Mandragora
Immense Mandragora.publicNotes:
A mandragora looks like a freshly pulled tuber that has grown into the malformed shape of a child with a grotesque face and hideously bloated body. Estos insidious little plants normalmente form when a mandrake root is watered with a demon's blood. Upon absorbing the otherworldly properties of the demon's blood, the root animates and is forced to seek out blood to feast from, lest it die of thirst.

Always famished and in search for sustenance, mandragoras live haunted, pained lives and perform vile and desperate acts to acquire the blood they crave. While they prefer magicaliado infused blood such as that of unicorns, fey, or sorcerers, and they can also feed off of potions, alchemical bombs, and other magical elixirs, a mandragora can subsist on the blood of non-magical criaturas. They find the flavor of mundane blood to be bland and bitter, and they do not blanch at voicing these complaints to la criaturas from which they drink.

While the typical mandragora is the size of a human child, some of these evil plants continue to grow and grow, reaching sizes more comparable to those of giants. Sometimes as they grow, they form additional limbs or rudimentary faces, eventualiado transforming into truly hideous mockeries of the human form.

Irahkatu.name: Irahkatu
Irahkatu.publicNotes:
The ahuizotl is a vicious, semi-aquatic predator that resembles a hideous cross between a badger and an otter, with disturbingly web-fingered paws supplemented by a fifth hand at el final de a long, serpentine tail. A clever and stealthy hunter, the ahuizotl lures unwary prey to their doom by mimicking the cries of people in distress. The ahuizotl's macabre habit of feeding on a victim's eyes, fingernails, and teeth leaves the corpses of its kills uniquely mutilated. Some say la criaturas consider these body parts delicacies, while others insist ahuizotls collect them as tribute to a powerful but unknown entity. The fact that an ahuizotl does not eat the actual flesh of its victims, instead depositing their savaged and waterlogged corpses in locations where the remains are sure to be found by friends or family, points to a third and perhaps more likely possibility-the ahuizotl simply enjoys using its violent dietary quirks to spread fear and despair.

An ahuizotl walks on all fours, but its hands are capable of manipulating simple tools and other objects. Ahuizotls have roughly mustelid features and an extra membrane covering their eyes, giving their eyes a dull color suggestive of cataracts and somewhat blunting la criatura's vision. Yet despite their bestial appearance, ahuizotls are nearly as intelligent as the average human, and wiser than most. Although they no form societies of their own, they have been known to aliado with violent cults or conclaves of monsters, and even to found small shrines and temples to sinister deities. The cult of Charon, the horseman of Death, is particularly popular among certain ahuizotls, who look forward to an afterlife spent wallowing in the waters of the River Styx.

Irovetti's Fetch.name: Irovetti's Fetch
Irovetti's Fetch.publicNotes:
Fetch stalkers form from the souls of Mediano or Pequeno fey or humanoids (Pequeno fetch stalkers have the same statistics as Mediano ones.)

A fetch is a twisted, deviant simulacrum of a humanoid criatura that exists or existed at one point on the Material Plane. Rumors of fetches that are reflections of entities from other planes persist, but none of these tales speak of fetches that duplicate anything other than a sapient source. A fetch can manifest spontaneously when a powerful criatura undergoes a significant emotional event or dies, either while on the First World or while in an area significantly influenced by the First World, but one can also be created by significant forces like the Eldest in order to torment and vex those who have annoyed them. While a fetch manifests from a soul's "reflection," and as such bears a striking resemblance to that criatura's appearance in life, a fetch has no true memories of its own. It keeps fragments of false remembrances from its source as if it experienced them in a half-remembered dream-which ensure the fetch is enraged by and jealous of its source.

A fetch is similar in appearance to la criatura whose soul spawned it, save that it often displays fey-like features such as pointed ears, plantlike elements, or supernatural grace. A fetch who seeks to impersonate a stillliving source must disguise these features, and takes care to manifest its fetch arma as one known to be wielded by its target.

When a fetch dies, it and its manifested items fades away into a bloom of plant life, its soul instantly recycled into the First World, leaving behind a patch of weeds and thorny flowers roughly in the shape they held in mockery while alive.

Jamandi Aldori.name: Jamandi Aldori
Jamandi Aldori.publicNotes:
Jamandi Aldori's upbringing in Restov could have ensured her a safe and relaxed life as one of that city's nobles, but her restlessness and frustration with "meddling" from the north increasingly pushed her away from the aristocratic lifestyle. She quickly mastered the art of the Aldori sword, and over the years has become one of Restov's most well-known swordlords, in part due to her skill in dueling, but of late as a result of her increasingly obvious pushes to expand Restov's power in directions that minimize reliance upon the rest of Brevoy. Beyond organizing the push into the Stolen Lands and her desire to foster a new aliado to the south, she hopes some day to found additional dueling schools beyond Brevoy's borders where the Aldori style can be taught-a pursuit that not all of her peers equitativamente approve of.

Characters who earn Jamandi's trust and support can unlock access to the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.vx5FGEG34AxI2dow.JournalEntryPage.cBBwTnJrVmvaRMYq]{Aldori Duelist} archetype at tu option.
